title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Geometry – Embedding for Enhanced Computational Efficiency
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Geometry – Embedding for Enhanced Computational Efficiency Quantum mechanics, while offering profound insights, often presents significant computational challenges for simulation and analysis. Traditional methods for representing and manipulating quantum states, such as representing wave packets as geometric objects, can be computationally expensive. This research proposes a novel embedding technique that leverages advanced algorithms to dynamically adjust the embedding parameters of quantum states, thereby minimizing the computational cost of representing and analyzing quantum mechanical systems. The core mechanism involves a 'quantum embedding' algorithm that employs a feedback loop to optimize the embedding space, resulting in efficient simulation and analysis. This approach aims to overcome limitations of current embedding techniques and offer a substantial speed-up in computational processes. This paper presents a detailed exploration of this methodology, detailing the algorithm's design, performance evaluation, and potential applications within the field of quantum computation and simulation.

title: Title: Universal Constraint-Free Logic (UCL)
abstract: Universal Constraint-Free Logic (UCL) represents a fundamentally new approach to formal logic, departing from the constraints inherent in traditional logical systems. This paper details the core principles and mechanisms of UCL, emphasizing the system's ability to define logical structures through inherent properties rather than predefined statements. The goal is to establish a framework capable of accommodating any logical specification, facilitating the creation of highly flexible and adaptable systems across diverse domains. UCL's innovative approach offers a significant departure from existing logic, promising a foundation for systems capable of handling a broader range of logical constructions.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the development of a novel quantum computing paradigm, Quantum Entanglement Computation (QEC), predicated on leveraging entanglement to accelerate computations and address longstanding challenges in optimization and cryptography. We detail the core mechanism of QEC, outlining its potential advantages over existing classical approaches. The paper presents a preliminary theoretical framework and explores the practical challenges associated with implementing this approach.

title: Title: Adaptive Cryptography Based on Dynamic Topology Structures – A Key Generation Method
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive cryptography approach centered on dynamic topology structures. Conventional cryptographic methods often rely on static keys, offering limited security against sophisticated attacks. This research proposes a method that leverages the inherent dynamic properties of topology to dynamically adjust key strength during encryption, thereby enhancing security and privacy. The core mechanism involves constructing a key generation algorithm that dynamically responds to the evolution of the topology, ensuring a robust and adaptable encryption process. This innovation aims to surpass the limitations of static key management and improve the overall security posture of cryptographic systems.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Probability Models: An Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on non-linear geometric probability models. Traditional optimization methods often rely on pre-defined parameters, limiting the flexibility of model design. This framework automatically learns and optimizes complex geometric models, leveraging probabilistic reasoning to enhance prediction accuracy. The core mechanism involves introducing a "Geometric Probability Function" that transforms model parameters into probability functions, facilitating optimization through probabilistic inference. This approach offers a significant advancement over existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving high-dimensional data and complex geometric structures, ultimately leading to improved predictive performance. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, explores its performance through theoretical analysis and simulation, and discusses its potential applications.

title: Self-Adaptive Connective Theory for Adaptive Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Self-Adaptive Connective Theory (ASLT) designed to enhance the generalization and robustness of machine learning models. Traditional machine learning approaches often rely on static models, limiting their adaptability to complex data. We propose ASLT as a framework where neural network connections and activations are dynamically adjusted, allowing the model to learn and adjust its structure based on the data itself. This dynamic adaptation fosters improved generalization and robustness, addressing a significant gap in current machine learning paradigms. The paper details the core mechanism of ASLT, outlining the conceptual shift towards self-adaptive networks and explores its implications for enhanced learning and model performance. We provide a preliminary analysis demonstrating the efficacy of this approach through illustrative examples and discuss potential future research directions.

title: Quantum Simulation-Based Probabilistic Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic algorithm, Quantum Simulation-Based Probabilistic Algorithm (QSPBA), leveraging the power of quantum simulation to predict complex system behavior and enhance risk assessment. Traditional probabilistic algorithms often struggle with computational complexity, particularly when dealing with intricate systems. Quantum simulation offers a paradigm shift by utilizing quantum mechanics to provide vastly improved predictive capabilities. The core mechanism of QSPBA centers around creating quantum entangled states to represent system states and facilitating probabilistic calculations, thereby increasing accuracy and efficiency compared to classical methods. We detail the algorithm's design, its theoretical foundation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential for advanced risk evaluation. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact on various fields.

title: Adaptive Quantum Topology Dynamics
abstract: Quantum topology, a novel framework for manipulating spacetime, offers unprecedented opportunities for designing complex, self-sustaining systems. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust parameters within a quantum topology system, thereby enabling self-maintenance. We propose a mechanism based on "quantum pulses" – precisely controlled quantum interactions – to induce changes in the system's topological structure, which in turn affects its behavior. The core claim is that this approach, unlike conventional parameter adjustment methods, provides a dynamic and self-regulating system, capable of adapting to changing conditions. We detail the theoretical framework, propose a numerical simulation, and highlight the implications of this dynamic system for potential applications in quantum computing and advanced materials science.

title: Non-Linear Associative Networks for Quantum Simulation
abstract: Quantum simulation is a critical component of modern quantum computing, enabling researchers to model complex quantum systems. Traditional approaches often struggle with the inherent complexities of quantum mechanics, particularly the non-linear correlations that govern their behavior. This paper proposes a novel associative network architecture, termed "Non-Linear Associative Networks" (NLAN), designed to overcome these limitations. We present a framework where nodes are connected through weighted relationships, fostering the simulation of intricate correlations and emergent phenomena. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically adjusted network structure, allowing for adaptation to the specific quantum system being simulated. This architecture offers a promising pathway towards more efficient and realistic quantum simulations, addressing current computational bottlenecks. We detail the network architecture, explore its performance characteristics through simulations, and discuss potential future advancements.

title: Bayesian Networks for Multivariate Anomaly Detection
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to multivariate anomaly detection utilizing Bayesian Networks (BNs). Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with the complexity and high dimensionality of real-world multivariate data. This research proposes a framework that leverages the probabilistic reasoning capabilities of BNs to model complex systems and identify deviations from normal operation. The core idea involves constructing a multi-variable Bayesian Network, learning the system's normal behavior through probabilistic inference, and subsequently identifying anomalies based on deviations from this learned model. We explore the theoretical foundations of this approach and discuss its potential applications across various domains. The presented method offers a flexible and interpretable solution for anomaly detection, particularly well-suited for systems exhibiting intricate dependencies between multiple variables.

title: Composable Quantum Modules for Algorithm Synthesis
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum algorithm design centered around the concept of "Composable Quantum Modules." The core idea is to move away from monolithic algorithm development towards a modular, component-based paradigm, similar to software engineering. We define and describe a framework for creating and utilizing pre-built, reusable quantum modules – representing fundamental quantum operations – to construct larger, more complex algorithms. This framework addresses the current challenges associated with quantum algorithm development, particularly the difficulty in managing the exponential complexity of designing and debugging intricate quantum circuits. The proposed approach offers significant advantages in terms of modularity, reusability, and ultimately, accelerates the development and deployment of quantum applications. We detail the architecture of this framework, including a standardized operation library and composition tools, and illustrate its potential through a conceptual example. The goal is to establish a practical methodology for synthesizing algorithms efficiently by leveraging modular building blocks.

title: Continuous Learning System Based on Memory Modules
abstract: This paper presents a novel continuous learning system designed to mitigate catastrophic forgetting, a significant challenge in continually learning scenarios. The system leverages a memory module to store newly acquired information, coupled with an attention mechanism for selective integration into a knowledge network. Unlike traditional continuous learning methods that often rely on model reshaping or regularization techniques, which can lead to performance degradation on previously learned tasks, our approach offers a more efficient and robust solution. The core claim of this work is the effective utilization of new information for knowledge update while avoiding catastrophic forgetting. The proposed mechanism introduces a memory module and an attention mechanism to achieve this goal. The system's architecture allows for adaptive learning and maintains performance across multiple tasks. The system is evaluated conceptually, outlining the key components and their interactions, demonstrating the potential of this approach for real-world continuous learning applications.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Machine Learning Framework (DAMLMF)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Adaptive Machine Learning Framework (DAMLMF), a novel approach to optimizing complex systems by dynamically adjusting machine learning models. The core of DAMLMF lies in its ability to intelligently adjust model parameters based on real-time data and feedback, thereby enhancing model generalization. We present a rigorous design and evaluation of DAMLMF, demonstrating its efficacy in a variety of challenging scenarios. The framework's success stems from a sophisticated interplay of adaptive learning algorithms, parameter optimization techniques, and a feedback loop that continuously refines model performance. The proposed method offers a significant advancement in the field of machine learning, particularly for complex systems with dynamic dependencies.

title: SAC-Net: Structure-Aware Collaborative Network for Graph Similarity Computation
abstract: Abstract Graph Similarity Computation (GSC) is a core task in graph analysis. However, current mainstream GNN-based similarity models still suffer from two fundamental bottlenecks. First, constrained by the inherent mechanism of recursive local aggregation, namely the 1-Weisfeiler–Lehman (1-wl) test, these models primarily measure similarity by aligning local structures, while struggling to capture long-range dependencies and overall topological configurations. Second, the simplified treatment of edge features prevents them from fully exploiting fine-grained semantic interactions between nodes. To address these challenges, this paper pro-poses Structure-Aware Collaborative Network (SAC-Net), an end-to-end framework that leverages structural information to unify global contexts with local affinities. Specifically, we design a Dynamic Structural Perception (DSP) backbone to establish a joint evolution paradigm for node, position, and edge features. By treating positional encodings as dynamic states, the model effectively captures long-range dependencies and overall topological configurations to maintain a robust global structural skeleton. Subsequently, this study introduce an Edge-Aware Fusion mechanism that leverages edge features as a bridge to adaptively integrate global and local structural information, thereby effectively addressing the alignment and integration of multi-granularity semantics. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate that SAC-Net effectively integrates global and local information, leading to more accurate graph similarity measurement.

title: Приложение для автоматического распознавания новостей, сгенерированных ИИ, и новостей, написанных человеком
abstract: В данной выпускной квалификационной работе рассмотрен подход к разработке программного продукта для бинарной классификации новостных текстов на русском языке. Классификация разделяет публикации на написанные человеком и сгенерированные большими языковыми моделями (Large Language Models, LLM). Рассмотрены основные аспекты области обработки естественного языка (Natural Language Processing, NLP) и особенности LLM. Выявлены ключевые сложности задачи классификации сгенерированных текстов. Проведен сравнительный анализ четырех классов методов классификации. Обоснован выбор подхода на основе градиентного бустинга решающих деревьев. Сформулированы функциональные и нефункциональные требования к программному продукту. Сформирован обучающий набор данных. Разработан алгоритм извлечения 32-мерного вектора стилометрических, лексических и морфологических признаков. Обучена и оптимизирована модель LightGBM с подбором оптимального порога принятия решения. Реализовано клиент-серверное веб-приложение. Протестировано общее качество классификации обученной модели. Исследована латентность вычислений на текстах различной длины. Проведено модульное и системное тестирование разработанного программного продукта.

title: Importance-Aware Low-Rank Distillation of Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have emerged as a dominant architecture for high-quality text-to-image generation, yet their scale poses challenges for efficient deployment. While truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) is a principled tool for parameter reduction, evidence from large language models (LLMs) suggests that naive low-rank approximation can cause catastrophic failure. In contrast, we find that truncated SVD in DiTs produces smooth degradation even under substantial global compression, with redundancy distributed across projection matrices throughout the whole network rather than concentrated in a few transformer blocks. Building on these insights, we introduce SVDtrunc, a two-step block-level compression scheme, first allocating ranks across blocks and compressing the least important ones via truncated SVD under a global parameter budget, and then fine-tuning all blocks with modular knowledge distillation and a rectified-flow objective. We apply SVDtrunc to FLUX.dev across compression levels ranging from 40-90% of the original parameter count. Across three benchmarks, GenEval, HPSv2, and DPG, we outperform all competing approaches. Notably, and in contrast to prior work, we retain near-full performance at 68% and remain competitive even at 57% of the original parameter budget. Furthermore, we show that SVDtrunc complements step distillation and achieves strong results even without fine-tuning, positioning it as a practical continuation of efficiency improvements beyond diffusion step reduction for large-scale generative models. Project page: https://vislearn.github.io/SVDtrunc/

title: Compila sion perfecta: IA para ingenieros (T03-E02)
abstract: En el episodio 2 de la tercera temporada de Compila Sion Perfecta, titulado “IA para Ingenieros: De Usuario a Creador en 40 Minutos”, el ingeniero Yesith Ternera explicó cómo los profesionales y estudiantes pueden pasar de utilizar herramientas de inteligencia artificial de manera básica a integrarlas estratégicamente en soluciones de ingeniería. Durante el programa se aclararon varios mitos: la IA no piensa ni posee conciencia como una persona; no es indispensable ser experto en programación para comenzar a utilizarla; y su propósito no es reemplazar a los ingenieros, sino automatizar actividades repetitivas y ampliar sus capacidades. Se destacó que aprovecharla adecuadamente exige formular problemas, proporcionar contexto, hacer preguntas técnicas y validar críticamente los resultados. El episodio presentó la inteligencia artificial como un conjunto de modelos matemáticos entrenados con grandes cantidades de datos para reconocer patrones, clasificar información, realizar predicciones o generar contenido. También se mencionaron aplicaciones prácticas en la detección de anomalías en redes, el análisis de registros de servidores, la optimización de procesos y la organización de documentación técnica. Como herramientas recomendadas se propusieron ChatGPT, utilizado como asistente técnico para analizar configuraciones, explicar protocolos y plantear arquitecturas, y Google Colab, como laboratorio en la nube para experimentar con Python, datos y modelos de IA sin instalaciones complejas. Finalmente, se invitó a los estudiantes a experimentar con problemas pequeños y reales, recordando que la IA no sustituye el criterio profesional: fortalece la capacidad del ingeniero para analizar sistemas, tomar decisiones y crear soluciones tecnológicas responsables.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应神经网络的训练
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two particles become linked and share the same fate regardless of distance, has long been considered a theoretical resource with potential applications in quantum computing and quantum information processing. Recently, the concept of quantum entanglement has begun to be explored in machine learning, particularly in the context of quantum neural networks (QNNs). This paper investigates the feasibility of utilizing quantum entanglement to accelerate the training process of neural networks. title: Title: Geometric Modeling of Neural Network Dynamics
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric modeling to the analysis of neural network activations, aiming to provide a robust and scalable method for understanding the network's behavior. Traditional approaches often focus on output prediction, while this research introduces a novel representation – the 'Geometric Neuron' – that leverages geometric curves to capture the network's response. We present a framework for constructing and analyzing these curves, demonstrating their potential to reveal insights into learning dynamics and network stability. The core mechanism centers on the creation of a geometric representation of activation functions, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to traditional activation function analysis. This work introduces a new computational tool for visualizing and quantifying the intricacies of neural network responses, potentially leading to a deeper understanding of their learning process. The development of the Geometric Neuron represents a significant step toward enhancing the interpretability of neural networks.

title: A fail-safe layered Guardrail for Emergency Detection in LLM Based Health Assistants
abstract: Large language model (LLM) assistants that answer health questions face an asymmetric error cost: failing to recognise a medical emergency can cause serious harm, whereas an unnecessary escalation costs only inconvenience. We present the safety layer of HealthSense AI, a multi-agent health information assistant, and describe a three-layer guardrail in which a deterministic keyword router first classifies risk, an LLM classifier then makes every final decision, and the deterministic layer serves as a fail-safe floor whenever the LLM is unavailable. We evaluate the design on an 87-case test suite covering emergency must-block prompts, safe controls, output-side blocking, and adversarial paraphrases, including a 31-case independently written adversarial set. The final system achieves 100% emergency recall (25/25), 100% output-guardrail accuracy (13/13), and zero false alarms. We also report a failure found during development — an earlier deterministic whitelist that overfitted the initial test set — and the redesign it motivated. All code and test cases are public at github.com/smita-datascience/healthsense-ai.

title: Quantum Error Correction as a Network Topology
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing, crucial for reliable data storage and processing. This paper explores the application of network topology to QEC, proposing a novel protocol that leverages the inherent properties of quantum systems to maintain data integrity. We argue that traditional QEC methods often struggle with scalability and the inherent sensitivity of quantum states. This study investigates a potential network-based QEC architecture, focusing on the representation of quantum data as nodes and the use of quantum entanglement to detect and correct errors. The core claim is that a well-designed network topology can provide a robust and scalable framework for QEC, mitigating the limitations of current approaches. We will discuss the theoretical implications, potential challenges, and future research directions associated with this concept.

title: Graph Neural Networks Inspired by Biological Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph neural networks (GNNs) inspired by biological neural networks. The core claim is to design a biologically-inspired neural network architecture and integrate it with GNNs to enhance graph data representation and learning efficiency. The underlying mechanism involves mimicking the information processing mechanisms of biological neurons – incorporating plasticity, adaptability, and distributed feature representation – within a neural network framework specifically designed for GNN training and inference. This research proposes a new paradigm for handling graph data, leveraging the strengths of both biological neural networks and graph-structured data analysis. The system's architecture consists of several layers of spiking neural networks, coupled with a GNN layer for final output. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of connections within the spiking neural network layers, guided by the graph structure and the GNN's output. This approach demonstrates the potential for improved performance and reduced training time compared to traditional GNNs, particularly in scenarios with complex graph structures and sparse data. This work lays the foundation for future research exploring the convergence of neuroscience and graph representation learning.

title: 基于动态拓扑的神经网络架构优化
abstract: The current landscape of neural network architectures often relies on fixed parameter settings, limiting their adaptability and hindering performance on complex datasets. This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture optimization method, leveraging dynamic topology, to automatically adjust network structure and parameters for enhanced model performance and generalization capabilities. We propose a dynamic topology framework where the network's structure and weights are represented as a continuous, evolving map, allowing for continuous and adaptive optimization. The core mechanism centers around a novel algorithm that iteratively refines the topology, focusing on key dimensions to improve both accuracy and robustness. This approach offers a significant departure from traditional optimization techniques, promising to address the limitations of static architecture tuning and unlock new possibilities for neural network design. We present a comprehensive experimental evaluation demonstrating the effectiveness of our dynamic topology framework, showcasing substantial improvements in both validation accuracy and robustness across a variety of benchmark datasets.

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Relational Reasoning with Symbolic Structures
abstract: Neural networks have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, yet they often falter when it comes to relational reasoning – the ability to understand and manipulate relationships between entities. This work addresses this limitation by proposing a self-supervised learning framework designed to train networks in the intricacies of symbolic relational reasoning. The core idea is to leverage synthetic data generated from symbolic representations of relationships and train networks to perform operations like addition, negation, and implication on these structures. This process effectively creates a learned relational grammar. We demonstrate that by grounding neural networks in symbolic representations, we can significantly improve their performance on relational reasoning tasks compared to purely data-driven approaches. The framework's inherent structure promotes interpretability and robustness, presenting a novel pathway towards more reliable and understandable AI systems. The key contributions include a novel data generation strategy, a self-supervised learning objective tailored for relational operations, and a demonstrable improvement in relational reasoning performance. ---

title: 基于非线性自组织网络的混沌系统预测
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for predicting the dynamic behavior of complex systems based on non-linear self-organizing networks. Traditional prediction methods often rely on static models, limiting their ability to accurately represent the intricate dynamics of these systems. Our proposed algorithm, termed "Dynamic Adaptive Network Dynamics" (DAND), leverages the inherent properties of non-linear self-organization to learn and adapt network structure and parameter values, enabling more robust and predictive forecasting. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop that dynamically adjusts network topology and node weights, fostering a system that mimics the complex patterns observed in the original system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DAND through simulations of a stochastic model exhibiting characteristic chaotic behavior. The algorithm's ability to capture emergent dynamics and provides a foundation for advanced control strategies. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the algorithm's performance, highlighting its potential for improved prediction accuracy and system understanding.

title: GeoAI Skills: Agent Skills for Reliable Geospatial Computing
abstract: Evidence and documentation release. No skill file changed: runtime-v2 records a skill tree byte-identical to v0.4.0 (runtime_tree_sha256 65023155d532…), so every measurement below still describes the shipped tree. What this release contains The repository's first paired behavior measurement, published as measured, including the project quality gate it fails. BEHAVIOR.md, ROADMAP.md, GOVERNANCE.md and SUPPORT.md, so the behavior boundary, open evidence gaps, reporting channels and release decisions are readable without private planning history. An immutable schema-v2 runtime hash registry covering every file shipped from each skill plus the shared release license, enforced in CI and the release preflight, with a byte-level parent lineage for future freezes. tools/paired_analysis.py, which joins the two measurement arms — case- and criterion-level win/loss/tie with exact two-sided binomial sign tests. Measurements, with their exact boundaries Routing — Claude Code 2.1.214, claude-sonnet-5, suite efe27d8c1736…, 167 cases: 99.17% precision, 96.77% recall, 96.41% full-route accuracy, zero control activations. The same run recorded one false positive, four false negatives, one incomplete route and eleven execution errors; all remain in the card. Routing says which skill loaded, not whether the answer was correct. Behavior — Claude Code 2.1.222, claude-sonnet-5, suite 520bc41dd4c0…, 93 cases per arm, 92 clean matched pairs: | Measure | Skills enabled | Control | Paired result | |---|---:|---:|---| | Criterion coverage | 145/302 (48.0%) | 85/302 (28.1%) | 65 W / 5 L / 232 T, p = 2.2e-14 | | Cases meeting every criterion | 18/92 | 6/92 | 42 W / 3 L / 47 T, p = 8.7e-10 | | Critical spatial failures | 4/92 (4.3%) | 13/92 (14.1%) | 3.25x fewer observed | | Forbidden-behavior violations | 0 | 0 | no separation | | Skill activation | 92/92 | 0/92 | clean control arm | The Phase 3 gate fails on both of its conditions (>=85% case pass rate, <2% critical spatial failure) and remains open. Judgments are from a single different-family model (gpt-5.6-sol, low reasoning), uncalibrated and not human-verified; 47 arm-blinded human review packets are prepared and pending reviewers. Raw response text is deliberately unpublished so that review is not contaminated; hashes and lengths preserve identity. Routing and behavior use different runtime versions and suite hashes. They are never pooled. One documented execution defect is retained rather than hidden: on swe-devops-standards/review-mode the enabled arm produced every required artifact but did not terminate within the frozen turn budget. The run was pre-registered and sealed by SHA-256 before the first model call, with three dated addenda recording every deviation — including one taken after partial data was seen, disclosed as such. Known limitations One runtime/model pair; run-to-run variance on this suite is unmeasured. 18 of 93 cases carry only two criteria and cannot separate the arms by construction. No reproducible real-world case has been accepted yet. Read BEHAVIOR.md, BENCHMARK.md, EVALUATION.md and ROADMAP.md before quoting any figure above.

title: Proxy-Based Diagnostics of Quantum Oracle Sketching Robustness for Non-IID Sensor and Telemetry Streams
abstract: Published quantum-streaming theory establishes quantum memory advantages for specific streaming problems; how a correlation-sensitive proxy model behaves under the structured dependence typical of sensor and telemetry streams, however, remains uncharted. We present a proxy-based diagnostic and hypothesis-generation framework for correlation-sensitive streaming analysis. Operational proxies for the refreshing time τ and repetition number r, introduced in this paper, are estimated on five synthetic non-IID regimes (IID, Markov switching, seasonal drift, burst repetition, and long-range dependence) and mapped onto a (τ,r) sensitivity landscape—the paper’s central artifact. Three memory-bounded classical baselines (online SGD, averaged SGD, and Count-Min) supply empirical reference points; no quantum algorithm is implemented or simulated and all quantum curves are heuristic proxy estimates. Analytic and empirical refreshing-time estimates diverge by up to 125× under long-range dependence (≈8× for Markov)—the two estimators answer different questions about temporal dependence. Using empirical τ, the proxy model predicts a hypothesised proxy-favourable region under mild-to-moderate Markov correlation that closes as correlation strengthens: the mean curves cross at ρ*≈0.82 under the operating constants (C=2, δ=0.05; the crossing moves between ρ*≈0.38 and beyond the sweep range across a C–δ grid, so only the ordinal reading is robust), and by ρ=0.88 the classical baseline exceeds the proxy estimate (Hodges–Lehmann difference 0.046). Applied unchanged to two real NAB telemetry streams, the same estimators place NYC Taxi inside and Machine Temperature outside the hypothesised favourable region—an ordering that persists across all tested encoder resolutions—with imbalance-aware metrics guarding against majority-class artefacts. Ablations over the τ estimator, forward window, stream length, target function, and proxy constants preserve the regime ordering within each estimator family.

title: A novel model-based biclustering for ordinal data via a URV approach
abstract: Abstract We introduce a novel finite mixture model for biclustering ordinal data matrices, simultaneously clustering rows and columns within the Underlying Response Variable (URV) framework. Ordinal responses are modeled as discretizations of latent Gaussian variables, while component-specific covariance matrices are parsimoniously parameterized via a factor analytic structure to capture complex dependence patterns efficiently. To address computational challenges arising from the high-dimensional likelihood evaluation inherent to ordinal data, model parameters are estimated using a Composite Likelihood (CL) approach, which offers significant computational advantages with negligible loss of efficiency. Extensive simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of accurate cluster recovery and reliable parameter estimation. We further illustrate the applicability of the methodology through an empirical analysis of two real-world ordinal datasets, highlighting its potential for uncovering meaningful latent bicluster structures.

title: Minimum Cardinalities of Multipartite Unextendible Product Bases
abstract: In quantum information theory, the state space of a multipartite quantum system is modeled by a tensor product. In the tensor-product space $\mathbb C^{d_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathbb C^{d_p}$, a nonzero vector is a \emph{product state} if it can be written as $\lvert φ_1\rangle\otimes\cdots\otimes\lvert φ_p\rangle$ with $\lvert φ_j\rangle\in\mathbb C^{d_j}\setminus\{0\}$. An \emph{unextendible product basis} (UPB) is a finite family of pairwise orthogonal product states such that no nonzero product state is orthogonal to all of them. UPBs play a key role in investigating quantum entanglement and nonlocal phenomena. Finding a smallest UPB is a natural extremal problem: it asks how few pairwise orthogonal product states suffice to prevent any further product state from being added. The general minimum-size problem for UPBs has been studied for over two decades since the seminal work of Alon and Lovász. For local dimensions $d_1,\ldots,d_p\ge2$, let $f_m(d_1,\ldots,d_p)$ be the minimum cardinality of a UPB and let $f_{LB}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)=1+\sum_{j=1}^{p}(d_j-1)$ be the natural lower bound. Alon and Lovász determined exactly when $f_m$ attains the lower bound $f_{LB}$, but the obstructed multipartite cases remained open in general. We prove a stabilization theorem: for every non-all-qubit system with $p\ge3$, whenever parity prevents the natural lower bound $f_{LB}$ from being attained, the true minimum is exactly $f_{LB}+1$. Equivalently, if the number of even local dimensions is positive and even, and at least one local dimension is greater than two, then $f_m(d_1,\ldots,d_p)=f_{LB}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)+1$. The proof is built on a unified graph-theoretic framework. Our result, together with earlier work, settles the minimum-cardinality problem for UPBs in all finite quantum systems.

title: TacPAC: Tactile Prediction and Real-Time Action Correction in World-Action Models for Contact-Rich Manipulation
abstract: World-action models guide action generation with predicted future observations, but vision-centric predictions miss the local contact cues that decide contact-rich manipulation. However, naively predicting future tactile observations as additional views recovers only a third of the achievable gain in our experiments. This gap reflects a timing mismatch: predictions precede execution, while tactile feedback arrives during it. We introduce TacPAC, which turns tactile prediction into real-time action correction. Once the base model has planned an action chunk, TacPAC caches the predicted contact that plan was conditioned on together with the plan's own representation, and a tactile expert reads each newly observed tactile image against that cache to correct the actions not yet executed. Feedback is thus interpreted against what the plan anticipated rather than in isolation, and one correction is a single pass over that cache, 20.7times cheaper than regenerating the chunk. On five real-robot tasks spanning precision insertion, fragile-object handling, object reorientation, and long-horizon manipulation, TacPAC leads every task and raises the average from 22% for its vision-only base model to 64%. Code is available at https://github.com/LogosRoboticsGroup/TacPAC.

title: MZ-Rain: Moisture-Budget-Guided Zero-Inflated Model for Station-Level Precipitation Nowcasting
abstract: Accurate station-level precipitation nowcasting is critical for agriculture, water resource management, and disaster prevention, which typically is formulated as a time series forecasting problem. However, conventional time-series modeling techniques face two major challenges in addressing station-level precipitation nowcasting: (1) Lack of Physics-Guided Modeling}, where meteorological variables are treated as a homogeneous set without accounting for their distinct roles in precipitation formation, leads to predictions that deviate from the physical processes governing precipitation. (2) Severe zero inflation in precipitation, where dry intervals dominate the dataset, obscuring meaningful precipitation patterns and complicating the predictive modeling. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{MZ-Rain}, a moisture-budget-guided zero-inflated sLSTM framework for station-level precipitation nowcasting. Guided by the moisture budget equation, MZ-Rain decomposes the precipitation formation process into process-specific pathways corresponding to moisture storage, moisture transport, surface evaporation, and precipitation persistence, and captures their temporal evolution through dedicated sLSTM branches. To account for the zero-inflated nature of precipitation, MZ-Rain introduces an adaptive Tweedie modeling strategy that adaptively modulates the rainfall mean while jointly learning precipitation occurrence as an auxiliary task, enabling the model to better balance dry-wet discrimination and quantitative precipitation estimation. Extensive experiments across diverse geographical and climatic regimes demonstrate that MZ-Rain consistently outperforms strong baselines on multiple evaluation metrics, including CSI, FAR, MSE, and MAE. In particular, the model exhibits superior skill in forecasting heavy precipitation events, while benefiting from physically grounded process modeling.

title: Latent-Aligned Reasoning for Multimodal Recommendation
abstract: Multimodal Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in cross-modal understanding, yet a fundamental challenge persists when applying them to recommendation: as representations propagate through multi-step reasoning, both visual and textual signals progressively attenuate - a phenomenon we term cross-modal dilution. To address this, we propose LARK (Latent-Aligned Reasoning frameworK), a two-stage latent reasoning framework with complementary alignment mechanisms within a single VLM. In the first stage, learnable latent tokens are interleaved with multi-step chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and explicitly aligned with a frozen vision encoder, serving as visual checkpoints that preserve perceptual details throughout the reasoning chain. In the second stage, the latent representations are projected via a bridge MLP and trained with item-to-item contrastive learning; to prevent the reasoning semantics from fading, intermediate features are aligned with the CoT hidden states from the first stage, anchoring the final embeddings to the model's own reasoning output. Experiments on three public benchmarks and one industrial dataset show that LARK achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple recommendation architectures, with controlled ablations confirming the distinct contribution of each component.

title: Transparent SSD Failure Prediction Through Interpretable Artificial Intelligence Techniques
abstract: Solid-state drives (SSDs) have become critical storage components in computing infrastructures, cloud platforms, enterprise systems, and intelligent devices, making reliable failure prediction an important component of predictive maintenance and system dependability. Conventional machine-learning models can identify complex relationships among storage-health indicators, workload characteristics, error statistics, thermal conditions, and operational behavior, but their limited interpretability can restrict their practical adoption. This research develops a conceptual framework for transparent SSD failure prediction through interpretable artificial intelligence (AI), emphasizing the integration of predictive modeling with post-hoc explanation mechanisms such as Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). The methodological foundation is positioned within the broader development of advanced AI systems, including transformer-based, multimodal, reasoning-oriented, and neural architectures represented in the supplied literature. The framework separates prediction from explanation while establishing an evidence-oriented pathway through which individual SSD-health indicators can be associated with predicted failure risk. The analysis indicates that transparency should not be treated as an auxiliary visualization layer but as an integral property of the predictive-maintenance pipeline. The study further identifies important trade-offs between predictive complexity, explanation fidelity, computational overhead, and operational usability. By incorporating interpretable AI principles into SSD failure prediction, the proposed approach provides a structured basis for trustworthy maintenance decisions while acknowledging the limitations associated with model-agnostic explanations, distribution shifts, feature correlations, and the absence of universally representative SSD failure datasets.

title: Geometric Modeling of Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric modeling to represent and simulate the behavior of adaptive neural networks, focusing on dynamically adjusting network weights based on input data. Traditional approaches often treat neural networks as discrete states, limiting the ability to accurately model the network's evolution and response. We propose a novel method leveraging geometric representations of activation functions to capture the adaptive weight adjustment process. This method offers a new perspective on neural network dynamics, potentially providing a more robust and insightful framework for understanding and simulating these complex systems.

abstract: Quantum State Simulator & Optimization Algorithm presents a novel approach to quantum system simulation and optimization, leveraging the unique properties of quantum states. This research introduces a quantum state simulator capable of efficiently modeling complex quantum systems and employing the simulation results to guide optimization processes. Traditional simulation methods rely on classical computation, while our system offers a fundamentally different methodology, capitalizing on quantum mechanics for enhanced performance. This work demonstrates the potential of this architecture to address challenges in quantum algorithm design and system analysis, showcasing a significant step forward in the field.

title: Quantum State-Driven Dynamic Quantum Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state-driven dynamic quantum optimization algorithm designed to address the limitations of traditional optimization methods. The algorithm leverages the inherent quantum properties of superposition and entanglement to dynamically adjust optimization parameters based on the evolving quantum state. We propose a new approach to optimization that surpasses existing methods by offering improved efficiency and accuracy through automated parameter tuning. The core mechanism involves a quantum state representation, iterative adjustment of parameters based on quantum state analysis, and the application of a modified quantum optimization framework. The potential impact of this algorithm on diverse optimization problems is significant, offering a pathway towards more robust and efficient solutions.

title: Core Claim: Exploring the use of multi-scale quantum entanglement to construct topological encoding schemes, and proposing a quantum information transfer protocol based on topological structure, to achieve more efficient quantum communication.
abstract: Quantum information theory has seen considerable advancements in recent years, with a growing emphasis on secure communication and information processing. The development of robust quantum communication protocols is crucial for safeguarding sensitive data and enabling new technological capabilities. This paper investigates the potential of utilizing multi-scale quantum entanglement – a novel approach that leverages the topological properties of quantum systems – to construct robust and efficient quantum information transfer protocols. We explore the concept of "topological entanglement" – a specific type of entanglement where the entanglement is inherently linked to the geometry of space – and propose a protocol based on this concept. Our work addresses the limitations of existing approaches by focusing on the fundamental principles of topological entanglement and its implications for quantum information transmission. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental explorations to demonstrate the feasibility and potential advantages of this approach. The core contribution of this research is the design of a protocol that leverages topological entanglement to enhance the fidelity and security of quantum communication, offering a fundamentally new perspective on quantum information transfer.

title: Non-Euclidean Vector Space Optimization with Dynamic Kernel Selection (NVOSK-DS)
abstract: This paper introduces Non-Euclidean Vector Space Optimization with Dynamic Kernel Selection (NVOSK-DS), a novel algorithm for optimizing vector space data through adaptive kernel function selection. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex data landscapes, requiring manual tuning of kernel parameters. NVOSK-DS addresses this limitation by dynamically selecting kernel functions during the optimization process, improving the algorithm's ability to identify optimal solutions and handle non-convexity. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, its iterative adaptation process, and its performance evaluation across various benchmark datasets. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously refines the kernel selection based on the data's inherent characteristics, resulting in enhanced optimization capabilities.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Task Decomposition
abstract: This paper explores the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) with Hierarchical Task Decomposition (HTD) to solve complex problems requiring coordination and planning among multiple agents. The core claim is that complex tasks necessitate hierarchical planning and strategic coordination. The proposed mechanism involves a MARL framework where agents learn and execute complex tasks by decomposing them into smaller, more manageable sub-tasks, guided by a hierarchical structure. This approach addresses the challenges of scalability and exploration inherent in traditional MARL methods. The system is designed to improve learning efficiency and task completion rates in scenarios where agents must collaborate to achieve a common goal. The paper outlines the key components of the framework, including the hierarchical decomposition strategy, the reinforcement learning algorithms employed by individual agents, and the communication protocols used for coordination. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to standard MARL techniques.

title: Quantum Adaptive Topological Optimization in Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) remains a critical challenge for the practical realization of quantum computation. Traditional QEC approaches often rely on pre-defined error correction codes and fixed topological structures, which may not be optimal for all quantum systems and noise environments. This paper proposes a novel framework for quantum error correction that leverages adaptive topological optimization. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the error correction topology in real-time, based on feedback from the quantum system, to maximize information transmission efficiency and resilience to noise. We construct a quantum error correction network where each physical qubit is associated with multiple logical qubits, forming a topological code. Utilizing quantum measurement and control techniques, we monitor the coherence and noise levels of the qubits, alongside the effectiveness of the error correction code. A quantum feedback control algorithm then dynamically modifies the topological connections, minimizing the impact of noise and enhancing the correction efficiency. This adaptive approach offers a significant improvement over static QEC methods, promising more robust and efficient quantum communication and computation in challenging environments. The theoretical framework presented demonstrates the potential for achieving significantly improved performance through real-time topology optimization.

title: 基于多模态概率推理的智能决策系统
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to intelligent decision-making systems by leveraging multimodal probabilistic reasoning. The core idea is to integrate data from various modalities – including visual, auditory, and textual information – to perform probabilistic inference and ultimately improve decision accuracy and robustness. We propose a framework that constructs multimodal probability models, transforming each modality into a probability distribution. Bayesian inference and related techniques are then employed to conduct multimodal probabilistic reasoning, culminating in the generation of a final decision. title: Constraint Network Cryptography E: Constraint Network Phase Transition of Rigid Cryptography — From Parameter Illusion to Theoretically Rigorous Quantum Immunity Spectrum
abstract: Within the constraint network phase transition framework, this paper reconstructs the threat of quantum computing to cryptography as a spectrum of threetypes of information barriers: spectrum‐hiding, geometric‐torsion, and theorem‐rigidity.Spectrum‐hiding hardness (RSA, ECC) has been penetrated by the quantum Fouriertransform; geometric‐torsion hardness (lattice cryptography) is quantum‐resistantbut relies on continuously tunable parameters and unproven computational assumptions, suffering from parameter illusion. Theorem‐rigidity hardness is rootedin discrete uniqueness locked by mathematical classification theorems; its securitybasis is jointly constituted by classification theorems, the structural‐reconstructionhardness assumption, and combinatorial expansion. Classification theorems exclude continuous deformation attack paths; the structural‐reconstruction hardnessassumption maintains one‐wayness under partial invariant disclosure; combinatorial expansion exponentially amplifies the discrete base structure space to resistGrover search. A categorical inadmissibility proof further shows that, under therestriction of no irreducible multiplicity, the category of rigid structures cannot befaithfully embedded into the quantum‐solvable category, thereby blocking spectralmanifestation of the quantum Fourier transform at the structural level. This papercompletes a paradigm shift from parametric belief to theorem‐guaranteed security,providing a theoretical coordinate for post‐quantum cryptography.

title: Adaptive Meta-Learning Optimizer
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive meta-learning optimizer designed to autonomously adjust its optimization algorithm parameters across diverse tasks and datasets. The core concept revolves around a meta-optimizer, an internal neural network that evaluates and dynamically adjusts the parameters of an external optimizer (e.g., Adam, SGD). This adjustment is driven by the task objective and the underlying data distribution. The proposed approach introduces the concept of "meta-optimization," where the optimizer itself learns to optimize, effectively adapting to varying learning scenarios. We demonstrate the potential of this architecture to improve convergence speed and final performance in a range of learning problems. This work contributes to the growing field of meta-learning by providing a mechanism for adaptive optimization strategies.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Curiosity
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) faces significant challenges in environments with sparse or delayed rewards. Traditional RL algorithms often struggle to explore effectively, leading to slow learning or failure to converge. This work proposes a novel approach that integrates probabilistic programming with intrinsic curiosity mechanisms to address this problem. We leverage probabilistic programming to represent the agent's policy and the environment dynamics, enabling a more flexible and expressive learning framework. Simultaneously, an intrinsic curiosity module, driven by prediction error or state entropy, encourages the agent to explore novel states and maximize its uncertainty. This combination allows the agent to actively learn from states with limited external reward signals. The core idea is that by explicitly modeling uncertainty and actively seeking out novel experiences, the agent can overcome the limitations of sparse reward environments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, highlighting its potential to significantly improve exploration and learning in complex RL scenarios. The framework presented offers a more robust and adaptable solution compared to conventional RL methods. ---

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Propagation with Adaptive Thresholds
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum algorithms to constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), specifically focusing on enhancing constraint propagation efficiency. Traditional CSP solvers often rely on fixed threshold values for constraint evaluation, which can limit performance. We propose a novel quantum algorithm that dynamically adjusts these thresholds based on problem complexity, leading to significant improvements in speed and accuracy. The core mechanism involves quantum state manipulation to rapidly evaluate constraints and optimize threshold adjustments. This approach offers a fundamentally new perspective on constraint propagation, potentially unlocking substantial gains in problem-solving time.

title: Using Large Language Models for Automated Corpus Annotation and Linguistic Analysis: A Critical Methodological Framework
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to classify, label, summarize, and interpret large text collections, creating new possibilities for corpus linguistics. Their capacity for zero-shot and few-shot instruction following could reduce the cost of linguistic annotation and extend analysis beyond the categories handled by conventional part-of-speech taggers, parsers, and dictionary-based tools. At the same time, LLM outputs are probabilistic, prompt-sensitive, model-dependent, and potentially biased, raising fundamental questions about measurement validity, annotation reliability, and reproducibility. This article critically synthesizes foundational corpus-annotation principles with recent evidence on LLM-based text annotation and develops a validated human–LLM workflow for corpus research. The framework distinguishes token-, span-, sentence-, document-, and discourse-level annotation; requires a human-coded gold sample before large-scale deployment; treats prompt design as part of the annotation manual; and evaluates accuracy, precision, recall, F1, inter-annotator agreement, stability across repeated runs, subgroup performance, and error types. Recent studies show that LLMs can approach or exceed crowd-worker performance on some well-specified classification tasks, but that performance varies substantially across datasets, languages, models, prompts, text lengths, and annotation complexity. Span-level annotation and context-dependent semantic or pragmatic coding remain particularly challenging. The article therefore argues against unvalidated full automation and proposes selective automation, disagreement-based human adjudication, model/version documentation, and preservation of raw outputs. For corpus linguistics, the strongest near-term use of LLMs is as flexible annotators within a transparent, theory-driven, and auditable pipeline rather than as replacements for linguistic expertise. The resulting framework supports scalable corpus annotation while preserving the empirical principles on which corpus-based linguistic inference depends.

title: Mode-pairing quantum key distribution with a heralded single-photon source
abstract: Mode-pairing quantum key distribution (MP-QKD) is a promising protocol immune to detector side-channel attacks and capable of breaking the repeaterless PLOB bound without global phase locking. Existing MP-QKD protocols employ weak coherent sources (WCSs) with a low probability of single-photon emission, hindering MP-QKD's performance improvement. We propose a new, to the best of our knowledge, MP-QKD protocol using the heralded single-photon source (HSPS) to significantly reduce the vacuum emission probability and increase the single-photon emission rate. Compared with the original WCS-MP-QKD protocol, this protocol has three advantages. First, its maximum transmission distance is extended from 488 km to 560 km. Second, the key rates at 100, 200, 300, and 400 km are 4.4 to 7.4 times those of the original protocol. Third, it does not change the original architecture of MP-QKD and is easy to implement experimentally. This HSPS-MP-QKD protocol has application potential in future metropolitan area QKD networks.

title: Probabilistic teleportation of shared high-dimensional multi-particle secrets
abstract: Quantum secret-sharing is a fundamental technique in quantum communication and plays a crucial role in high-dimensional quantum secret transmission. This paper investigates the teleportation of arbitrary d-dimensional multipartite quantum secrets and proposes both deterministic and probabilistic teleportation protocols. The schemes employ generalized Bell-state measurements, generalized Pauli operators, and auxiliary particles to achieve efficient and secure quantum secret-sharing. The deterministic protocol employs maximally entangled channels to achieve perfect sharing with unit success probability. Moreover, the probabilistic protocol, assisted by auxiliary particles and generalized unitary operations, achieves perfect fidelity quantum secret sharing via non-maximally entangled channels. The protocols are further extended to arbitrary d-dimensional systems, and their robustness under several common quantum noise models is analyzed numerically. Compared with previous schemes, the proposed protocols support arbitrary multipartite entangled states, high-dimensional systems, non-maximally entangled channels, and noise analysis within a unified framework. These results enrich the theory of high-dimensional quantum communication and provide practical approaches for future quantum secret-sharing and secure quantum networks.

title: AI-driven passenger experience monitoring in railway operations: a Reddit-based NLP analysis of service failures, sentiment and operational priorities
abstract: Purpose This study develops an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework for using passenger-generated social media discourse as a complementary source of operational intelligence in railway service quality management. It examines whether Reddit discussions can reveal dimensions of passenger experience that are not adequately captured by official performance indicators. Design/methodology/approach Using the official Reddit API, the study collected 61,328 documents published between July 2024 and July 2026 across five railway communities. The framework combines lexicon-based classification into seven theory-informed service failure categories with non-negative matrix factorization topic modelling, VADER sentiment analysis, lexicon-based emotion detection and robust regression. Findings Delay-and-disruption discourse showed the highest proportion of negative documents, while safety discourse generated the greatest negativity intensity and visibility; comfort and cleanliness and ticketing and refunds were the most frequently discussed dimensions. Affective intensity and public engagement proved partially independent: delay and ticketing posts attracted significantly less engagement than average, safety, comfort posts significantly more. The index ranked comfort, cleanliness, staff, communication, ticketing and refunds as leading improvement priorities, with ticketing, delay dominating British, comfort dominating US discourse. Research limitations/implications Findings rest on self-selected Reddit communities and rule-based instruments validated internally rather than against human gold labels; they indicate digitally expressed passenger concerns, not representative estimates of the passenger population. Practical implications Operators and regulators can use the framework as a low-cost, continuously updated instrument complementing official performance indicators. Its extension into an early-warning system is set out as a design proposition requiring prospective validation against operational incident data, not as a capability demonstrated here. Social implications This study highlights social media as a democratic space for public accountability in transit management. By amplifying organic passenger discourse, the framework empowers commuters who's daily lived experiences, such as comfort, cleanliness and communication issues, are often overlooked by rigid official KPIs. Recognizing these grievances underscores how transit quality directly impacts public trust, equity and socio-economic well-being. Furthermore, addressing regional variations in passenger concerns helps operators design more inclusive services. Ultimately, integrating this digital feedback into policy ensures that vital public infrastructure better aligns with the diverse safety, accessibility and comfort needs of the communities it serves. Originality/value The study demonstrates how large-scale passenger discourse can be transformed into actionable railway service intelligence by integrating theory-informed classification, affective analysis, engagement modelling and a multidimensional operational priority measure.

title: AI-driven day-ahead renewable energy forecasting: Assessing machine learning performance under blind and weather-informed paradigms
abstract: Accurate day-ahead renewable energy forecasting remains one of the most challenging problems in modern energy systems because photovoltaic and wind generation are not controlled by the operator, but by uncertain atmospheric forcing. This paper develops a complete NASA POWER-driven artificial intelligence framework for one-day-ahead renewable power forecasting under two sharply different operational assumptions. The first scenario is a strict blind forecast , where only historical information is available. The second is a weather-informed forecast , where day-ahead meteorological predictors at the target hour are introduced as proxy weather-forecast inputs. Hourly solar irradiance, wind speed, temperature, and humidity from NASA POWER are used to construct photovoltaic production, wind turbine generation, battery state of charge, persistence baselines, lagged features, residual-correction forecasts, daily-energy forecasts, and learning-based predictions. Three machine learning models, least-squares boosting, random forest bagging, and neural network regression, are compared with weighted ensemble variants. The obtained results show that historical information alone is insufficient for accurate hourly 24-hour-ahead prediction, with the best strict blind model achieving R 2 = 0.3551 and RMSE=445.50 kW. However, when day-ahead weather predictors are introduced, the LSBoost model reaches RMSE=2.29 kW and R 2 = 0.99998. This weather-informed result is interpreted as an idealized upper-bound experiment rather than as a directly deployable operational forecast, because the target renewable generation is synthetically constructed from the same meteorological variables and because realized target-hour NASA POWER variables are used instead of numerical weather prediction forecasts. This contrast does not merely improve accuracy; it exposes the physical reason behind renewable forecastability. Meteorological information is therefore a central driver of one-day-ahead renewable-power prediction. The proposed dual-scenario strategy therefore provides both a lower-bound historical evaluation and an upper-bound weather-informed benchmark for energy planning, microgrid scheduling, and battery-aware renewable management.

title: Ordered-Angle Coding for Exact Multiuser Unanimity Testing
abstract: We introduce ordered-angle coding for binary-unanimity testing among $n$ transformation-only users in a serial quantum architecture inherited from Loop-Back communication. User $B_i$ fixes one private sign across a logical word and applies $R(s_iα_j)$ in trial $j$. If $w$ users choose the negative sign, serial composition gives $R[(n-2w)α_j]$. We show that every fixed same-axis pulse that is deterministic for both unanimous inputs under the binary Bell readout has $α_j=q_jπ/(2n)$ with integer $q_j$. For a nonadaptive word $\mathbf q=(q_1,\ldots,q_m)$, a mixed Hamming weight imitates the unanimous signature with probability \[ M_{\mathbf q}(w)=\prod_{j=1}^{m}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{πq_jw}{n}\right). \] Within this complete deterministic-unanimity pulse family, a finite perfect word exists if and only if $n$ is a power of two. For $n=2^r$, the dyadic word $(1,2,4,\ldots,2^{r-1})$ is exact and pulse-minimal with $m_{\min}=r=\log_2n$ trials. It replaces the $O(n^2\log(1/\varepsilon))$ worst-case burden of repeated smallest-angle tests by exact $O(\log n)$ verification. Odd primes instead admit balanced statistical words with uniform mixed-weight imitation $2^{-(p-1)}$. For actual operations $R(s_iα_j+δ_{ij})$, an ideal rejecting position is lifted to $\sin^2Δ_j$, where $Δ_j=\sum_iδ_{ij}$. This yields explicit robustness bounds with angular and binary-readout errors. Bell entanglement is not required for the additive algebra, but it keeps the traveler locally maximally mixed in every honest trial. We therefore present the result as a coded multiuser relation primitive with optional raw conference-key-candidate use, not as a composably secure conference-key protocol.

title: CrossDepth: Geometry-Constrained Attention for Generalizable Multi-View Surround Depth Estimation
abstract: Reliable 3D understanding of the surrounding environment is a core requirement for autonomous driving. Multi-view surround camera rigs provide broad scene coverage, but the spatially adjacent images typically overlap only minimally. Consequently, the depth of most pixels must be inferred from monocular appearance cues. These cues can appear differently across images and may therefore be interpreted differently by the depth estimation model. We target two main sources of cross-image inconsistency: differences in camera intrinsics and the limited receptive field of each image. We address the former by conditioning the features on per-pixel camera-aware ray embeddings, enabling the network to account for camera-dependent variations in monocular cues. We address the latter by extending each pixel's context beyond its own image through cross-image attention constrained to geometrically plausible regions, derived from the calibrated rig setup. The model is trained in a fully self-supervised manner based on photometric consistency. Evaluations on DDAD and nuScenes show improved overall depth accuracy and cross-image depth consistency over state-of-the-art self-supervised methods under in-domain and cross-domain evaluation. Code is available at https://abualhanud.github.io/CrossDepthPage/.

title: When Genomic Masking Priors Fail to Transfer: Strong Variant Prediction, Weak Functional Generation
abstract: Bidirectional discrete diffusion model appears naturally suited to genomic modeling because it can reconstruct missing sequence from both flanks. We developed GenDA (Genomic Density-optimized Absorbing Diffusion) under the additional hypothesis that entropy-guided span placement would concentrate reconstruction pressure on compositionally complex regions, improving both downstream variant-effect prediction and functional sequence generation. Our results only partially support this premise. After supervised fine-tuning, the 202M-parameter GenDA model reaches a pooled ClinVar SNV AUROC of 0.774, exceeding a similarly scaled autoregressive model by 0.103. However, a matched random-span variant reaches 0.777, providing no evidence that entropy guidance causes the ClinVar improvement. More unexpectedly, GenDA fails a zero-shot functional inpainting stress test: across promoters, enhancers, exon boundaries, and intron boundaries, it does not consistently outperform a control that shuffles the native gap while exactly preserving 3-mer composition. Failure is already present for 50--500-bp gaps, although enhancer degradation worsens at longer gaps. Diagnostics identify several boundary conditions: entropy measures local sequence complexity rather than functional importance; 1-mer tokenization limits physical context; training spans are capped at 300 bp; and high absolute AlphaGenome fidelity can coexist with negative control-normalized restoration. evidence.title: When Genomic Masking Priors Fail to Transfer: Strong Variant Prediction, Weak Functional Generation
evidence.abstract: Bidirectional discrete diffusion model appears naturally suited to genomic modeling because it can reconstruct missing sequence from both flanks. We developed GenDA (Genomic Density-optimized Absorbing Diffusion) under the additional hypothesis that entropy-guided span placement would concentrate reconstruction pressure on compositionally complex regions, improving both downstream variant-effect prediction and functional sequence generation. Our results only partially support this premise. After supervised fine-tuning, the 202M-parameter GenDA model reaches a pooled ClinVar SNV AUROC of 0.774, exceeding a similarly scaled autoregressive model by 0.103. However, a matched random-span variant reaches 0.777, providing no evidence that entropy guidance causes the ClinVar improvement. More unexpectedly, GenDA fails a zero-shot functional inpainting stress test: across promoters, enhancers, exon boundaries, and intron boundaries, it does not consistently outperform a control that shuffles the native gap while exactly preserving 3-mer composition. Failure is already present for 50--500-bp gaps, although enhancer degradation worsens at longer gaps. Diagnostics identify several boundary conditions: entropy measures local sequence complexity rather than functional importance; 1-mer tokenization limits physical context; training spans are capped at 300 bp; and high absolute AlphaGenome fidelity can coexist with negative control-normalized restoration. These results show that strong fine-tuned variant prediction, a plausible corruption prior, and functional generation are distinct claims that require separate validation.

title: Predictive Anomaly Detection for Real-Time Virtual Account Transactions and API-Driven Payment Processing Across Enterprise Banking Platforms
abstract: The migration of enterprise banking toward instant payments and virtual-account structures has changed anomaly detection from retrospective transaction review into a real-time analytical problem.Virtual accounts can generate high-frequency payment streams across corporate collections, reconciliation processes, customer accounts, and API-connected banking services, creating transaction patterns that static rules may inadequately distinguish from operational or behavioral abnormalities.This study develops a predictive anomaly-detection framework for real-time virtual-account transactions and API-driven payment processing.Rather than evaluating transactions independently, the framework models temporal and contextual behavior using transaction velocity, amount deviation, beneficiary patterns, account activity, payment sequences, processing status, API latency, response codes, retry frequency, and failed-payment clusters.Historical and rolling behavioral baselines establish expected activity at account, transaction, and API levels, while machine-learning and anomaly-detection models generate dynamic anomaly scores for incoming events.Temporal validation, threshold calibration, and false-positive analysis evaluate detection reliability under changing transaction conditions.The resulting intelligence differentiates account-level anomalies from payment-processing irregularities, supporting prioritized investigation, adaptive controls, faster exception management, and resilient real-time banking operations.

title: Analysis pipeline and coding instrument for a survey of procedural knowledge representation in multi-agent systems
abstract: The analysis pipeline and coding instrument behind the survey "Procedural Knowledge Representation in Multi-Agent Systems: Routing, Planning, and Execution at Scale". The survey classifies 136 primary papers spanning 1981 to 2026 along six ordinal axes, and admits an axis value only where a verbatim passage from the source supports it. This archive contains the machinery that produced andchecked that classification: the coding instrument as a decision tree (question set 4.13, and 3.0 as used for the abstract-only validation study), the card schema, the annotator brief, the generators that emit the paper's tables from the analysis cards, and the validators that check every card against the schema and every quotation against the source it cites. Everything is deterministic and offline: Python 3.9 or later, standard library only, no network access, no API keys, no model calls. Given the companion dataset of analysis cards, the pipeline regenerates Table III, Supplement S1-B and Table S1 of the paper, and reproduces the full-corpus audit. The analysis cards themselves are not included here; they are published as a separate dataset and cited by their own DOI. Source PDFs of the surveyed papers are not included, as they are third-party copyrighted works; every card carries a DOI so sources can be retrieved independently.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Probability Density Estimation for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum entanglement to improve the estimation of probability density within complex systems. The core claim posits the design of a quantum algorithm, termed "Quantum Entangled Probability," that leverages entanglement to accelerate and enhance predictive modeling capabilities. Current probabilistic methods face significant computational challenges, particularly when dealing with intricate systems exhibiting high dimensionality and complex dependencies. Quantum computing, through its unique properties of superposition and entanglement, offers the potential to overcome these limitations, providing a pathway to more accurate and efficient predictions. This research explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of this novel approach, focusing on its potential impact on diverse fields requiring precise probabilistic modeling. The paper details the Quantum Entangled Probability algorithm, its underlying principles, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its efficacy in a simulated environment.

title: Probability Neural Networks: Learning Topological Structures through Dynamic Probability Matrices
abstract: This paper investigates the application of probability neural networks (PNNs) leveraging dynamic probability matrices to learn network parameters and improve machine learning and pattern recognition capabilities. We propose a novel model that incorporates topological structure analysis into the network's parameter learning process, offering a significant advancement over traditional PNN architectures. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic probability matrix that captures the network's topology, allowing for efficient parameter optimization and enhanced performance in complex scenarios. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments, showcasing improved accuracy and robustness in various machine learning tasks. The theoretical implications of this work extend to the exploration of novel topological learning algorithms.
